citations.title: Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act
citations.requirement: Governing statute. The article list shows Art. 6 (licensure, §§1796.32-.41), Art. 7 (HCO operating requirements, §§1796.42-.43), Art. 8 (affiliated aides, §§1796.44-.45), Art. 10 (complaints/inspections, §§1796.51-.54), Art. 11 (enforcement, §§1796.55-.59). The sections fetched contain no staffing ratios, no client-rights or grievance rules, no records-retention period and no emergency-plan rule.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: (a) An affiliated home care aide is 18 or older, is EMPLOYED by an HCO, and is listed on the registry. (j) An HCO arranges home care services by an affiliated aide. (n) 'Home care services' are NON-MEDICAL services for a client who cannot perform them because of age or disability. They include bathing, dressing, feeding, exercising, hygiene/grooming, transferring, ambulating, positioning, toileting/incontinence care, assisting with self-administered medication, housekeeping, meals, laundry, transportation, correspondence, phone calls, shopping and companionship. Aides may NOT assist with medication that would otherwise require administration or oversight by a licensed health care professional. (i) The registry is a public CDSS website.

citations.title: Entities that are not home care organizations
citations.requirement: Exempts licensed home health agencies and hospices, IHSS providers, employment agencies referring independent aides, and DDS-vendored organizations (per research S9). Used to define who is and is not an HCO.

citations.title: HCO licensure requirements and two-year renewal
citations.requirement: (a)(2)-(4) Proof of $1M/$3M liability insurance, workers' compensation (policy number, dates, carrier name and address) and a $10,000 employee dishonesty bond with third-party coverage. (a)(5) On request, give CDSS a complete list of affiliated aides and proof each meets §§1796.43, .44 and .45. (a)(6) Licensee passes the §1796.33 background exam. (a)(7) Licensee completes the CDSS orientation. (a)(8) No outstanding fees or civil penalties. (a)(9)-(10) Disclose prior roles in licensed facilities and any discipline. (a)(11) Board members understand their duties. (a)(13) Cooperate with CDSS. (b) Renew every 2 years, fee postmarked on or before expiration. (c) CDSS mails a fee notice at least 60 days before the renewal date.

citations.title: Denial, suspension and revocation
citations.requirement: Grounds to deny, suspend or revoke an HCO license (carried from fact-checked research S12; section text not re-fetched in this pass).

citations.title: Posting of license and business hours
citations.requirement: Post the license, business hours and any other information CDSS requires at the place of business in a conspicuous location visible to both clients and affiliated aides.

citations.title: Workers' compensation
citations.requirement: Maintain and abide by a valid workers' compensation policy covering affiliated aides.

citations.title: Employee dishonesty bond
citations.requirement: Maintain and abide by an employee dishonesty bond, including third-party coverage, of at least $10,000.

citations.title: General and professional liability insurance
citations.requirement: Maintain proof of general and professional liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 aggregate.

citations.title: Abuse reporting and report retention
citations.requirement: Report suspected or known dependent adult/elder abuse as required by WIC §15630. Report suspected or known child abuse as required by Penal Code §§11164-11174.3. Keep a copy of EACH suspected-abuse report, available to CDSS for review during normal business hours.

citations.title: Registry clearance before client contact; staff clearance; TB; notice on separation
citations.requirement: Aides must be cleared on the registry before direct client contact. (a)(1) Any staff person, volunteer or employee with contact with clients, prospective clients or confidential client information must satisfy §§1796.23, .24, .25, .26 and .28 BEFORE that contact or access. (a)(2) Aides must show they are free of active TB under §1796.45. (b) The licensee may require criminal record clearance of exempt individuals who have client contact.

citations.title: Notify CDSS when an aide is no longer employed
citations.requirement: Immediately notify the department when the HCO no longer employs an individual as an affiliated home care aide.

citations.cite: HSC §1796.44(a)-(d) (in effect through 12/31/2026; reenacted by SB 412, Stats. 2025, ch. 414)
citations.title: Affiliated home care aide training
citations.requirement: The licensee must ensure each aide completes training BEFORE providing services. (b) Minimum 5 hours entry-level training before presence with a client: 2 hours orientation on the aide's role and the terms of employment, and 3 hours safety (basic safety precautions, emergency procedures, infection control). (c) Plus a minimum 5 hours of annual training, core-competency and population-specific. It must include clients' rights and safety, daily living needs, reporting/preventing/detecting abuse and neglect, personal hygiene help, and safe transport if transportation is provided. (d) Training may be online.

citations.title: Dementia training added to annual training
citations.requirement: From 1/1/2027 the annual training must also cover the special care needs of clients with dementia. The 5-hour entry and 5-hour annual minimums are unchanged. The bill digest also describes dementia training prior to providing care and annually thereafter; the chaptered §1796.44(c)(6) text lists it in the annual training. Counsel should confirm whether a pre-service dementia component is required.

citations.title: Tuberculosis examination of aides
citations.requirement: (a) Aides hired on or after 1/1/2016 must be examined 90 days before employment or within 7 days after. (b) The exam is a CDC-recommended, FDA-licensed TB infection test and, if positive, a chest X-ray. The aide may not work unless the licensee has documentation from a licensed medical professional of no risk of spreading disease. (c) Repeat at least every 2 years if negative. Once a positive test has been followed by an X-ray, repeat exams are no longer required. (d) After each exam the aide submits, and the HCO keeps on file, the practitioner's certificate. (e) The exam is a condition of initial and continuing employment. (f) A transferring aide meets the requirement with a certificate from within the past 2 years, or verification from the prior HCO that it holds the certificate and a copy is provided before the aide starts.

citations.title: License fees
citations.requirement: Initial (24-month) and renewal fees set by the department. Current schedule per CDSS (research S2): HCO license $5,603 per 2 years, change of location $100, change in corporation $200, aide registration $35.

citations.title: Complaint procedures
citations.requirement: CDSS may establish procedures for the receipt, investigation and resolution of complaints against HCOs.

citations.title: Inspections, complaint investigations, abuse cross-reporting
citations.requirement: (a) CDSS may investigate complaints. (b) CDSS verifies compliance through random, unannounced inspections. (c) Inspections may cover books, records and premises. Refusing access is cause for license revocation. (d) CDSS has no oversight of registered aides other than maintaining the registry. (e) On receipt of an abuse report under §1796.42(e), CDSS cross-reports to local law enforcement and APS (adult victim) or CPS (child victim). It has no duty to investigate beyond that.

citations.title: Department entry during business hours
citations.requirement: CDSS may enter an HCO during posted business hours, with or without advance notice (per research S49).

citations.title: Elder and dependent adult abuse mandated reporting
citations.requirement: (a) Persons with full or intermittent responsibility for the care or custody of an elder or dependent adult, whether or not paid, including any elder or dependent adult care custodian, are mandated reporters. (b)(1) Report observed, known or reasonably suspected physical abuse, abandonment, abduction, isolation, financial abuse or neglect, or abuse disclosed by the elder/dependent adult. Report by telephone or confidential internet tool immediately or as soon as practicably possible. A written or internet report follows within 2 working days. (b)(1)(F) For abuse outside a long-term care facility, the report goes to the adult protective services agency or local law enforcement.

citations.title: Paid sick leave
citations.requirement: Paid sick leave of at least 40 hours / 5 days per year (per research S36).

citations.title: Employer indemnification of employee expenses
citations.requirement: The employer must reimburse necessary employee expenditures, including mileage for driving between clients and on client errands (per research S37). The 2026 IRS rate is 72.5 cents per mile (S38), a common benchmark.

citations.title: Third-party employers and the companionship/live-in exemptions
citations.requirement: Third-party employers of home care workers, including HCOs, may not claim the FLSA companionship or live-in exemptions from minimum wage and overtime.

citations.title: Electronic visit verification for Medicaid personal care services
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid-funded personal care services. It applies only to Medi-Cal-funded visits. Confirm the system with DHCS or the managed care plan.

citations.cite: CDSS HCS 281 — Application Instructions for an HCO License (Sections A and B)
citations.title: Required application content: personnel policies, training plan, job descriptions, program description, HCS 308 designee
citations.requirement: B2 job descriptions for each position. B3 personnel policies covering hiring, discipline, grievance and mandated reporting, stating that employment is conditional on fingerprint clearance, a criminal-conviction statement, TB clearance and registry listing. B4 training plan with trainers, objectives and a sample log. B5 program description (services, area, hours, population, assignment/supervision). B6 insurance certificates. HCS 308: at least one designee, and a licensee cannot designate him/herself; LLC/corporations attach a board resolution. HCS 402 bond.

citations.cite: CDSS Home Care Services application fees and HCO/HCA application pages
citations.title: Fees, forms, HCSB and Care Provider Management Branch contacts
citations.requirement: HCO license $5,603 per 2 years; change of location $100; change in corporation $200; aide registration $35 per 2 years and $35 renewal. HCSB: (877) 424-5778, HCSB@dss.ca.gov, 744 P Street, M.S. 9-14-90, Sacramento, CA 95814. Aide Live Scan/registration via the Guardian portal (Care Provider Management Branch 1-888-422-5669, guardian@dss.ca.gov).

citations.cite: CDSS/DHCS joint notice (Dec. 16, 2021) — Medi-Cal Personal Care Agencies serving the HCBA Waiver
citations.title: HCBA Waiver Personal Care Agency exemption from HCO licensure
citations.requirement: Medi-Cal Personal Care Agencies providing HCBA Waiver Personal Care Services are exempt from HCO licensure. An HCO that is not enrolled for the waiver is not covered by this exemption.

citations.cite: DHCS Community Supports Policy Guide, Vol. 1 (updated April 2025) — Personal Care and Homemaker Services (PCHS)
citations.title: Medi-Cal managed care Community Supports
citations.requirement: PCHS is a plan-offered Community Support. It covers eligibility, IHSS as the primary program, HCBA exclusion and provider types. Plans contract with and pay providers. Pricing benchmark (non-binding) $29/$33/$38 per hour (research S19).

policies.title: Job Description — Licensee, Administrator and Designee (HCS 308)
state_specifics: Duties: day-to-day operation, compliance with the Act, insurance and bond upkeep, registry and TB oversight, and reporting to CDSS
HCS 308 names at least one designee to act in the licensee's absence; a licensee cannot designate him- or herself
An LLC or corporation attaches a board resolution to HCS 308
Supervision given: Client Care Supervisor, Scheduler/Coordinator, volunteers
Supervision received: governing body or owners (if any); CDSS oversight

policies.title: Job Description — Client Care Supervisor
state_specifics: Duties: client assessments, service plans, aide assignment and supervisory visits
The Act sets no supervisor credential or ratio; set the qualifications and caseload as an operator standard
Supervision given: affiliated home care aides
Supervision received: Administrator/designee
Must state who covers when the supervisor is absent

policies.title: Job Description — Scheduler / Registry and Billing Coordinator
state_specifics: Duties: scheduling, missed-visit follow-up, timekeeping, billing, registry and Guardian entries
Confirms an aide is registry-cleared before the first assignment
Gives immediate notice to CDSS when an aide leaves (HSC §1796.43(a)(3))
Supervision received: Administrator/designee
Staff with access to confidential client information must be background-cleared first (HSC §1796.43(a)(1))

policies.title: Job Description — Affiliated Home Care Aide
state_specifics: Aide is 18 or older, employed by the HCO, and listed on the Home Care Aide Registry
Duties: non-medical home care services as defined in HSC §1796.12(n), per the client service plan
Duties exclude assisting with medication that would require a licensed professional's administration or oversight
Supervision received: Client Care Supervisor
Supervision given: none

policies.title: Job Description — Volunteers and Other Classifications; Lines of Supervision Chart
state_specifics: HCS 281 B2 requires a job description for every classification, including volunteers and board members if they have client contact
Volunteers with client contact or access to confidential client information must be cleared before contact (HSC §1796.43(a)(1))
The organization chart must show who supervises whom
Each description states the supervision given and to whom, and the supervision received and from whom

policies.title: Hiring Practices and Conditions of Employment
state_specifics: Tell every applicant in writing that employment is conditional on fingerprint clearance, a statement of prior criminal convictions, TB clearance and registration on the Home Care Aide Registry
Affiliated aides must be 18 or older
TB exam is a condition of initial and continuing employment (HSC §1796.45(e))
Give CDSS a complete aide list and proof of compliance on request (HSC §1796.37(a)(5))
Use LIC 508 for the criminal record statement

policies.title: Employee Responsibilities to Report Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation
state_specifics: Employees are told in writing of their duty to report under HSC §1796.42(e)
Elder and dependent adult abuse: report under WIC §15630 to adult protective services or local law enforcement
Report immediately or as soon as practicably possible by phone or confidential internet tool; a written or internet report follows within 2 working days
Child abuse: report under Penal Code §§11164-11174.3
Keep a copy of each report available to CDSS during normal business hours; CDSS cross-reports to law enforcement and APS/CPS

policies.title: Home Care Aide Qualifications, Registry and Guardian Registration
state_specifics: Affiliated aide: 18 or older, employed by the HCO, listed on the CDSS registry
Registration through the Guardian portal ($35 per 2 years, $35 renewal) or HCS 100 by mail
Affiliated aides enter the HCO's PIN; the HCO may submit through its own Guardian account
No direct client contact before registry clearance
Care Provider Management Branch: 1-888-422-5669

policies.title: Background Checks (Live Scan) and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Any staff person, volunteer or employee with contact with clients, prospective clients or confidential client information must satisfy HSC §§1796.23, .24, .25, .26 and .28 before that contact or access
Live Scan runs through CDSS Care Provider Management Branch (guardian@dss.ca.gov)
The licensee may require criminal record clearance of exempt individuals who have client contact (HSC §1796.43(b))
The licensee must pass the §1796.33 background exam
Operator standard: re-screen against any additional exclusion lists required by contracted payers

policies.title: Employee Health and Tuberculosis Screening
state_specifics: Exam within 90 days before hire or within 7 days after hire
Exam is a CDC-recommended, FDA-licensed TB infection test and, if positive, a chest X-ray
Aide may not work until a licensed professional documents no risk of spreading disease
Repeat at least every 2 years if negative; no repeat once a positive test has been followed by an X-ray
Keep the practitioner's certificate on file; a transferring aide may rely on a certificate less than 2 years old or prior-HCO verification

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Each aide file holds registry status, Live Scan clearance, TB certificate, training logs and criminal-conviction statement
The file must support the proof of compliance CDSS may request (HSC §1796.37(a)(5))
TB certificate stays on file after each exam (HSC §1796.45(d))
The Act sets no retention period; adopt and state one (operator standard)
Keep files secured and separate from client records

policies.title: Wage, Hour, Overtime, Travel Time, Mileage and Paid Sick Leave
state_specifics: An HCO is a third-party employer and may not claim the federal companionship or live-in exemption
Paid sick leave: at least 40 hours / 5 days per year (Labor Code §246)
Reimburse necessary expenses, including mileage between clients and on client errands (Labor Code §2802); the 2026 IRS rate is 72.5¢/mile (benchmark)
Travel between clients during the workday is paid time (DOL guidance)
Pay at least the 2026 state minimum ($16.90) or the higher local minimum; have counsel review California daily overtime and live-in or 24-hour care

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: No borrowing money, accepting gifts or taking over client finances (see CR-04)
No assisting with medication beyond self-administration support
No private side arrangements with clients outside the agency
Confidentiality and social-media rules
Operator standard: HCS 281 B3 requires personnel policies; the Act sets no conduct rule

policies.title: Discipline and Employee Grievance Procedure
state_specifics: HCS 281 B3 requires personnel policies on hiring, discipline, grievance and mandated reporting
Progressive discipline steps with a written record
Employee complaint channel to the Administrator/designee, with no retaliation
Immediate removal from client contact pending investigation of abuse, neglect or exploitation allegations
CDSS may deny, suspend or revoke a license on the grounds in HSC §1796.38

policies.title: Aide Separation and Notice to CDSS
state_specifics: Notify CDSS immediately when the HCO no longer employs an individual as an affiliated aide (HSC §1796.43(a)(3))
Update the registry through the Guardian account
Return client keys and records; reassign affected clients
If the aide transfers to another HCO, TB verification may be shared under HSC §1796.45(f)
Exit checklist is kept in the personnel file

policies.title: Training Plan for Affiliated Home Care Aides
state_specifics: Submit the training plan to CDSS with the application (HCS 281 B4)
For entry-level and annual training, state who will conduct the training, written objectives, and title and duration of each course
The licensee must ensure each aide completes training before providing services
Training may be online (HSC §1796.44(d))
Include a sample training verification log (see TRN-05)

policies.title: Entry-Level Training (5 Hours Before Client Contact)
state_specifics: Minimum 5 hours before presence with a client
2 hours orientation on the aide's caregiver role and terms of employment
3 hours basic health and safety, including infection control and emergency procedures
Record completion in the training log before the first assignment
Operator standard: add a supervised competency check on core tasks

policies.title: Annual Training (5 Hours Per Year)
state_specifics: Minimum 5 hours annually, core-competency and population-specific
Required topics: clients' rights and safety
How to provide for and respond to daily living needs
How to report, prevent and detect abuse and neglect
How to assist with personal hygiene and other home care services; safe transport of a client if applicable

policies.title: Dementia Care Training (Effective January 1, 2027)
state_specifics: From 1/1/2027 annual training must also cover the special care needs of clients with dementia (HSC §1796.44(c)(6), SB 412)
The 5-hour entry and 5-hour annual minimums are unchanged
Counsel should confirm whether a pre-service dementia component is required
Update the training plan and log before 1/1/2027
Operator standard: assign the dementia module first to aides serving clients with dementia

policies.title: Training Verification Log and Training Records
state_specifics: Log fields: employee name; hire date; position title; registration date
Training title and brief description of topics
Month/day/year completed and hours received
Instructor first and last name (in-person); organization delivering the training
Location of training, or website if online

policies.category: B5. Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.title: Home Care Organization Program Description
state_specifics: Describe services, service area, hours, client population, and how aides are assigned and supervised
Services are non-medical only (HSC §1796.12(n))
State whether you serve only private-pay clients or also Medi-Cal plan clients
Update the description and notify CDSS when it changes materially
Entities exempt under HSC §1796.17 are not covered by this program

policies.category: B5. Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.title: Business Hours and Posting of License
state_specifics: State the business hours in the program description
Post the license, business hours and any other CDSS-required information conspicuously, visible to clients and aides (HSC §1796.42(a))
CDSS may enter during posted business hours, with or without notice (HSC §1796.53)
State after-hours and on-call contact arrangements for clients and aides
Notify CDSS of any change of hours or location; change of location fee is $100

policies.category: B5. Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.title: Basic and Optional Services; Scope — What Aides May and May Not Do
state_specifics: Basic services: bathing, dressing, feeding, exercising, hygiene/grooming, transferring, ambulating, positioning, toileting/incontinence care
Optional services: housekeeping, meals, laundry, shopping, correspondence, phone calls, companionship, transportation
Aides may assist with self-administered medication only
Aides may not assist with medication that would require administration or oversight by a licensed health professional
Skilled nursing and therapy require a different license; do not advertise or provide them

policies.category: B5. Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.title: Transportation Services and Safe Transport of Clients
state_specifics: Transportation is a listed home care service (HSC §1796.12(n)); the program description must say whether it is offered
If offered, annual training must cover safe transport (HSC §1796.44(c))
Operator standard: require a valid license, vehicle insurance and a safe-vehicle check for aides who transport
Reimburse mileage under Labor Code §2802
Operator standard: seat belts, wheelchair securement, and no transport against client or family wishes

policies.category: B5. Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.title: Procedure for Response to Abuse Reporting Duties
state_specifics: Aides and staff report observed, known or reasonably suspected elder or dependent adult abuse under WIC §15630
Report by phone or confidential internet tool immediately or as soon as practicably possible; written or internet report within 2 working days
Report suspected child abuse under Penal Code §§11164-11174.3
Make and keep a copy of each report, available to CDSS (HSC §1796.42(e))
The administrator ensures the report was made, protects the client, and documents follow-up; CDSS cross-reports to law enforcement and APS/CPS

policies.category: B5. Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.title: Service Area — Counties and Areas Served
state_specifics: List the counties or areas where clients are served; attach a map if needed
Do not accept clients outside the stated area without updating the program description
Consider aide travel time and mileage cost when setting the area
Advertising must match the licensed program and area
Licensure is from the CDSS Home Care Services Branch; HCSB (877) 424-5778

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Licensee and Designee Responsibilities
state_specifics: The Act sets no administrator license or RN requirement
The licensee must pass the background exam and complete the CDSS orientation
HCS 308 names at least one designee; the licensee cannot designate him- or herself
Board members sign HCS 9165 before joining; the licensee ensures they understand their duties (HSC §1796.37(a)(11))
HCS 309 lists owners, members and officers; keep it current

policies.title: Licensure, Renewal, Fees, Changes and Advertising
state_specifics: License term is 2 years; fee is $5,603 (non-refundable), same fee at renewal
Renewal fee must be postmarked on or before expiration; CDSS mails a fee notice at least 60 days before
Change of location $100; change in corporation $200
No outstanding fees or civil penalties at renewal (HSC §1796.37(a)(8))
Advertise only licensed non-medical services; display the HCO license number

policies.title: Required Insurance, Workers' Compensation and Employee Dishonesty Bond
state_specifics: General and professional liability: $1,000,000 per occurrence / $3,000,000 aggregate (HSC §1796.42(d))
Workers' compensation covering affiliated aides, kept in force
Employee dishonesty bond with third-party coverage of at least $10,000; HCS 402 names the State of California as beneficiary
Calendar renewals; a lapse violates operating requirements
Give certificates to CDSS on request

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Operator standard: review the manual at least annually and after any change in the Act
Track version, date and approver of each policy
Update the personnel policies and training plan on file with CDSS when they change
Known pending change: dementia training from 1/1/2027
Retire superseded versions with the date

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: The Act sets no QA program; this is an operator standard
Review incidents, complaints, missed visits and supervisory-visit findings quarterly
Track aide registry status, TB due dates and training hours
Track client satisfaction and corrective actions
Report results to the licensee/governing body

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Bill only for hours actually worked; EVV applies to Medi-Cal-funded visits
Do not bill for services outside the scope of home care services
A plan contract may require a compliance program and exclusion screening
Keep the dishonesty bond in force
Violations may lead to license action under HSC §1796.38

policies.title: CDSS Inspections and Complaint Investigations
state_specifics: CDSS verifies compliance through random, unannounced inspections
Inspections may cover books, records and premises; refusing access is cause for license revocation
CDSS may enter during posted business hours with or without notice
CDSS may investigate complaints (HSC §§1796.51-.52)
Designate a staff member to receive inspectors; keep records readily accessible

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: The Act has no client-rights list, so this is an operator standard
Annual aide training must cover clients' rights and safety (HSC §1796.44(c))
Rights include dignity, informed choice, freedom from abuse and exploitation, and privacy
Give the rights statement at intake and have the client or representative sign
Include how to reach CDSS HCSB (877) 424-5778

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: CDSS may investigate complaints (HSC §§1796.51-.52)
Give clients a written complaint process and the CDSS contact (HCSB@dss.ca.gov)
Operator standard: acknowledge in writing and resolve within set days
No retaliation
Log every complaint for QA review

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Staff with access to confidential client information must be background-cleared first (HSC §1796.43(a)(1))
HIPAA applies if the HCO is a covered entity or business associate (e.g., electronic billing to plans)
Give a notice of privacy practices if a covered entity
Minimum-necessary access; secure electronic and paper records
Breach response steps

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Financial abuse of an elder or dependent adult is reportable under WIC §15630
Operator standard: no gifts, loans, wills or power of attorney for staff
Written receipts for shopping and errand money
Aides do not access bank cards or PINs
Report suspected exploitation within the abuse-reporting timelines

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: No discrimination by race, color, national origin, disability, age, religion or sex
Provide reasonable accommodations for disabilities
Offer interpreter or translated documents to limited-English clients
Applies to payer-funded and private-pay clients alike
The Act sets no language rule; this is an operator standard

policies.title: Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: The Act sets no contract terms; this is an operator standard
The agreement states services, schedule, rates, minimum visit length and cancellation terms
State the scope limits and non-medical status
Give the client a copy before services start
Explain billing and how to dispute it

policies.title: Client Intake, Eligibility and Assessment
state_specifics: Accept only clients whose needs fit non-medical home care services
Refer clients needing skilled care to a licensed home health agency
Assess needs, home safety, medication-assistance needs and the client's emergency contacts
Check the service area and staffing before accepting
Operator standard: the Act sets no assessment form or timeline

policies.title: Service Plan and Plan Updates
state_specifics: The plan lists tasks drawn from HSC §1796.12(n) services
The plan lists the schedule and any transportation
Operator standard: review at set intervals and on change of condition
Aides receive the plan before the first visit
Plan changes are signed by the client or representative

policies.title: Supervision of Caregivers and Supervisory Visits
state_specifics: The Act sets no supervisory-visit frequency or supervisor ratio; this is an operator standard
The program description must say how aides are assigned and supervised (HCS 281 B5)
The Client Care Supervisor conducts and documents visits
Observe aide performance and client satisfaction
Address concerns found through corrective action and training

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
state_specifics: Aides may assist only with self-administered medication (HSC §1796.12(n))
Aides may not assist with medication that would require administration or oversight by a licensed health care professional
Aides may remind, open containers and hand the client the medication; the client takes it
Aides do not set up, adjust doses or give injections
Document assistance and report refusals or errors to the supervisor

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: Operator standard: aide late or absent → scheduler arranges coverage and notifies the client
Only registry-cleared aides are assigned
Document every missed visit and its cause
Backup aides trained on the client's plan
After-hours contact number is given to every client

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
state_specifics: EVV is required for Medicaid (Medi-Cal) personal care services; it does not apply to private-pay visits
Confirm the EVV system with DHCS or the managed care plan
Record actual start/stop times, including travel time between clients
Review exceptions and correct them with a documented reason
Time records support wage-hour compliance

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: Entry-level safety training covers emergency procedures (HSC §1796.44(b))
Call 911 for any emergency, then the supervisor
Aides give no medical treatment beyond first aid
Report any change in condition to the supervisor the same day; update the plan
Complete an incident report (see SAF-02)

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: The Act sets no discharge rule; this is an operator standard
Give written notice with reasons and a transition plan
Make safety referrals when care needs exceed non-medical services
Notify family or the representative and, if involved, the payer
Document the discharge and keep the record

policies.title: Coordination with Medi-Cal Programs and Other Payers
state_specifics: IHSS pays individual providers, not agencies; IHSS providers are not HCOs (HSC §1796.17)
PCHS is a Community Support offered by Medi-Cal managed care plans; plans contract with and pay providers
DHCS pricing resource is non-binding: $29/$33/$38 per hour
An HCO not enrolled for the HCBA Waiver is not covered by the PCA exemption
Federal HCBS settings rules apply only to HCBA/Medicaid HCBS-funded services; EVV applies to Medi-Cal visits

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Annual training covers how to report, prevent and detect abuse and neglect
Reporting procedure is in PRG-05 and PER-02
Clear aides before client contact
Respond to every allegation immediately and document it
Operator standard: remove the accused aide from the client pending review

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: The Act has no general incident-report form or deadline; this is an operator standard
Abuse reports under WIC §15630 carry their own deadlines (phone immediately; written within 2 working days)
Aides report falls, injuries and property loss to the supervisor the same day
The supervisor completes an incident form and follows up
Trends are reviewed under GOV-05

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Entry-level safety training includes infection control
TB screening of aides under HSC §1796.45
Hand hygiene and gloves for personal care
Provide protective equipment and a sharps/exposure procedure if the OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard applies
Staff with symptoms of contagious illness do not work with clients

policies.title: Client Emergency and Disaster Plans
state_specifics: The Act has no emergency-plan rule; this is an operator standard
Entry-level safety training covers emergency procedures
Prepare an emergency plan per client: contacts, evacuation help, medication list
Contact high-risk clients after disasters such as wildfire or earthquake
Keep a backup way to schedule and communicate

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: Workers' compensation must cover affiliated aides (HSC §1796.42(b))
Safe lifting and transfer techniques
Aides may leave an unsafe home and call the supervisor
Report injuries the same day
Operator standard: California employers may also owe a written injury and illness prevention program; confirm with counsel

policies.title: Client Records and Retention
state_specifics: The Act sets no records-retention period; adopt one (operator standard)
CDSS inspections may cover books and records, so keep them accessible
Contents: agreement, assessment, service plan, visit notes, incident reports, complaints
Keep abuse-report copies available to CDSS in business hours (HSC §1796.42(e))
Secure storage with limited access and a retention-and-destruction schedule

policies.title: Required Reports and Notifications to the State
state_specifics: Immediate notice to CDSS when an aide no longer works for the HCO
Abuse reports to APS/law enforcement/CPS, with copies retained
Notify CDSS of a change of location ($100) or change in corporation ($200)
Give CDSS a list of affiliated aides and proof of compliance on request
License renewal every 2 years, postmarked on or before expiration

required_items.text: Job Description for each classification (including employees, volunteers and Home Care Aides) with specific tasks or duties for each position. Must address: Duties and responsibilities
Job Description for each classification, must address: Lines of supervision (Must include supervision given and to whom, as well as, supervision received and from whom)

Personnel Policies – Abuse Reporting Procedures: At a minimum, documentation must indicate that employees will be informed of their responsibilities to report to appropriate agencies per Health and Safety Code Section 1796.42.

Personnel Policies – Hiring Practices: Documentation must include informing employees that conditions of their employment include fingerprint clearance, statement of prior criminal convictions, TB clearance, and registration on the Home Care Aide Registry.

Training Plan for Affiliated Home Care Aides, submitted to CDSS at the time of application. For both entry-level and annual training, the plan must include proposals on who will be conducting the training, written description of the objectives, and the title and duration of the training as specified in Health and Safety Code Section 1796.44.

Entry-Level Training: An Affiliated Home Care Aide must complete a minimum of five (5) hours of entry-level training prior to presence with a client. Training must include: Two (2) hours of orientation training regarding his/her role as a caregiver and terms of employment; and Three (3) hours of basic health and safety training, including but not limited to: Infection Control; Emergency Procedures

Annual Training: A minimum of five (5) hours of annual training that relates to core competencies and is population specific. Proposed training must include but not be limited to these topics: Clients rights and safety; How to provide for and respond to a client's daily living needs; How to report, prevent, and detect abuse and neglect; How to assist a client with personal hygiene and other home care services; and How to safely transport a client (if applicable).

Sample training verification log must be included with the training plan. At a minimum, the log must include: employees name; hire date; position title; registration date; training title and brief description of topics covered; month/day/year training was completed; training hours received; Instructor/trainer first and last name (if in-person training); organization delivering the training; and location of training (if online, please specify website).
Home Care Organization Program Description – element: Business Hours
Program Description – element: Description of the basic and optional services provided by the Home Care Organization which includes but is not limited to transportation services
Program Description – element: Procedure for response to abuse reporting duties
Program Description – element: Description of counties/area where clients are served (attach map if necessary)

official.notes: HCS 281 is an application booklet. No separate policy checklist form or regulation lists the required written policies for HCOs. The booklet itself says regulations are still being developed, with Written Directives to follow. Applicants mail one complete packet to CDSS Home Care Services Branch, 744 P Street, Sacramento, CA 95814 with the fee. The Section A forms and Section B supplemental documents must go in the same sequence as the booklet lists them. CDSS returns the whole packet if it is incomplete. The booklet requires original signatures and dates, and tells applicants to keep a photocopy. The Section B order is B1 (organizational documents), B2 Job Descriptions, B3 Personnel Policies, B4 Training Plan, B5 Program Description, B6 (insurance). So organize the manual as separately tabbed B2–B5 documents, with B1 and B6 handled as other application paperwork. The booklet gives no item numbers inside B2–B5. The IDs above (B2(a), B3(a), B4(a) and so on) are my labels for the bullets in the document's own order. B3 says Personnel Policies 'should include' the abuse-reporting and hiring items. The booklet notes that CDSS does not enforce other agencies' rules, such as minimum wage and Fair Employment Practices, but applicants should check for conflicts. B5 allows the program description to be a pamphlet, brochure or other document as long as all four elements are included. The booklet says nothing on discipline, medication, disaster plans, complaint procedures or similar topics, so I did not add any. The 8/15 B4 text may predate current training rules (HSC §1796.44 as amended by SB 412), so check the current HCS 281 and the statute.
